::: {.cite-bar .domain-war-powers}
[Repealed]{.status .status-repealed} [Pub. L. 107-243]{.cite} [116 Stat. 1498]{.cite} [50 U.S.C. 1541 note]{.cite}
:::

Authorized the President to use the armed forces to defend U.S. national security against the continuing threat posed by Iraq and to enforce relevant U.N. Security Council resolutions. It was the domestic legal basis for the 2003 invasion.

## Key provisions

- Sec. 3(a): authority to use force against the threat posed by Iraq and to enforce Security Council resolutions.
- Sec. 3(b): presidential determination that diplomacy alone would not protect the United States.
- Sec. 3(c): declared itself specific statutory authorization under the War Powers Resolution.

## Why it matters

Long after the Saddam Hussein government fell, the executive branch cited it as supplementary authority, including for the January 2020 strike on Qassem Soleimani. That use drove the repeal effort that finally succeeded through [the annual NDAA](ndaa-annual.qmd).

## Current status

Repealed by the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026 (Pub. L. 119-60), signed December 18, 2025. It was the first repeal of a war authorization since the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution was repealed in 1971.
